v1.feedback: The twilight palette ramp (amber → lavender → indigo) and per-bulb guttering sell the gloaming concept well, and the heavier gravity sag is a smart structural morph. However the chain transformation is mostly chromatic — push the form harder: let the differential-growth curve bifurcate or fray at the ends as twilight deepens, so the structure itself dissolves, not just the color. The single catenary reads thin in a 40k-particle budget; consider splitting into 3-5 parallel strands at different droop phases to fill more frame and echo Gonzalez-Torres' multi-strand installations. The z-axis is nearly unused (pressure + noise alone won't produce visible depth), so add intentional z-spread to give the orbit controls something to reveal.

v2.feedback: Fraying probability is vanishingly low (FRAY_PROB×0.04≈0.5%) and branches cap at 4, so the gloaming dissolution at strand ends barely registers before growth saturates — raise fray rate and let sub-branches sag more steeply to sell filaments dying into dusk. Palette transition (amber→lavender→indigo) should be keyed to growth progress, not just wall-clock time, so twilight deepening feels structurally earned. The five-catenary Gonzalez-Torres silhouette reads immediately and the guttering per-bulb flicker is a strong touch — but consider dimming the additive glow falloff more aggressively at late stages so the piece actually reaches near-darkness rather than plateauing at a warm haze.
